Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can validate that Redwood meets EdgeFin's performance requirements:

What we heard you prioritize:
- 99th percentile latency target: <= 350ms for single-turn text generation at 512 tokens (peak traffic)
- Sustained throughput: 1,000 qps (short bursts up to 2,500 qps) across 16 concurrent workers
- Streaming: low-latency chunked streaming for partial tokens with end-to-end latency < 200ms for first bytes
- KV-cache reuse expected for prompt prefixing across sessions

Next steps we propose:
1) You share the canonical prompt set and a representative token distribution (you can attach to this thread or use the Drive link).
2) We'll run a reproducible benchmark using Redwood's benchmark harness (we'll share methodology + scripts).
3) Joint validation window: 24-48h test with your sample traffic patterns; we'll instrument and share full traces and token-level cost breakdowns.

I've looped in Neha (SE) to outline the benchmark methodology and Vivek (solutions) for the deployment/capacity plan. Rafael will follow up on procurement/timing.

Attachments: edgefin_benchmark_requirements.xlsx (xlsx) — feel free to add columns for concurrency/percentiles you want measured.

If that plan looks good, can we lock in a 48h window next week starting Tue 3/9?

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications before we hand over the prompt set: 

- Streaming: When you say 'first bytes < 200ms' — is that measured from request arrival at the Redbox endpoint to first token sent, or from the client receiving the first chunk? We need client-observed numbers (including network within our VPC).
- Concurrency model: Our clients open long-lived connections (up to 16 concurrent) with requests arriving in bursts. We care about sustained p95/p99 across the 24h window, and worst-case p99 during burst periods.
- Measurement definitions: please confirm how you compute p99 (windowing, interpolation) and whether you include queue time before the model starts computing.

Also, please send the exact benchmark harness (script + docker image or commit hash) so our infra team can review reproducibility. We'll attach our canonical prompt set once we see the harness expectations.

Thanks —

Hi Alex / Priya —

Appreciate the clarifying questions — below is a concise overview of the benchmark methodology we'll use and the artifacts we'll share. I've attached our benchmark methodology PDF and an editable Excel for the prompt/traffic matrix.

Summary of measurement definitions (what we'll report):
- Client-observed latency: measured from request egress at your client to first token received (we instrument TCP timestamps and the client-side SDK). This is the number we'll use for the <200ms first-byte target.
- Server-side latency: time from request arrival at Redwood edge to model output start — we'll report this as a breakdown (queue time, scheduling latency, model compute).
- Percentiles: p50/p90/p95/p99 measured over fixed 1-minute aggregation windows across the run. For p99 we'll use standard interpolation on the empirical CDF per-minute, and we will also report a global/unwindowed p99 for the full run.
- Throughput: sustained qps measured as successful completed requests/sec (excluding rate-limited or errored requests). Bursts will be measured in 1-minute and 5-minute windows.
- Concurrency: we'll simulate long-lived connections with configurable keep-alive; concurrency counts active requests in-flight, not connection count.
- Streaming: client-observed time-to-first-chunk and time-between-chunks; we'll surface token-per-chunk sizes and any rebuffering events.

Reproducibility and harness info:
- We'll provide the benchmark harness as a Git commit (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness, commit: a1b2c3d) and a Docker image (redwood/benchmark:20260302).
- The harness supports configurable network delay (to model VPC egress), token distributions, and prefix caching. We'll include an exact seed and a sample traffic replay file generated from your attached prompt set.
- All scripts will emit raw traces (per-request JSON lines), aggregate summary CSVs, and a reproducibility README with the exact command line we ran.

Attachments:
- redwood_benchmark_methodology.pdf (detailed definitions + reproducibility checklist)
- edgefin_benchmark_requirements.xlsx (updated with requested measurement columns)

Ask from you: please confirm the token-distribution column in the attached workbook (we left example columns for 16/32/64/512 token buckets) and confirm whether network egress time inside your VPC should be treated as part of the client-observed latency (if you prefer we can run with a 5ms synthetic egress to emulate your infra).

If that looks good, we'll stand up the benchmark harness and propose a 48h window (Tue 3/9 -> Wed 3/10) and a time to review results live.

Thanks,
